issues.legal_issue: A tenant cannot establish ownership by adverse possession merely by occupying land beyond the area demised to them while the tenancy continues.
material_facts: The occupants’ tenancy under the previous owner was established by their evidence and the rent note.
The occupants claimed ownership by adverse possession and occupied some land beyond the portion included in their lease.
The purchasers sought a declaration of title and possession, and the lower courts found in their favour.
issues.conclusion: The occupants could not claim title by adverse possession merely because they had encroached on land beyond the leased portion while they were tenants; the purchasers were entitled to possession.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act, the Court held that occupation of additional land by persons who were tenants did not, on these facts, enable them to claim title by adverse possession. The Court relied on no earlier case for this issue.

rule.if: title_based_possession_suit and tenancy_established and encroachment_beyond_leased_area and adverse_possession_claim_based_on_tenancy_occupation

predicates.title_based_possession_suit: The proceeding sought possession on the basis of the claimant’s title.
predicates.tenancy_established: Evidence established that the occupants held the property as tenants.
predicates.encroachment_beyond_leased_area: The occupants possessed land beyond the area included in their lease.
predicates.adverse_possession_claim_based_on_tenanc: The occupants relied on their possession during the tenancy to claim ownership by adverse possession.

issues.definition: When a title-based possession proceeding concerns occupants whose tenancy is established and whose adverse-possession claim rests on occupying land beyond the leased area during that tenancy, the claim does not defeat the owner’s possession claim.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory rent-protection defence that was not raised in the lower courts cannot be introduced for the first time in a special-leave appeal when it depends on disputed facts, particularly where the suit seeks possession on the basis of title.
material_facts: The occupants denied that they were tenants and asserted that they owned the property by adverse possession.
The purchasers brought the suit for declaration of title and possession, rather than as an eviction suit under the Rent Act.
The occupants did not plead rent-protection entitlement in their written statement, and no such issue was framed or raised in the courts below.
The occupants sought to rely in the special-leave appeal on rent-protection provisions, including a provision introduced during the proceedings.
The occupants had denied the purchasers’ title, and that denial was found proved.
issues.conclusion: The rent-protection contention could not be considered at that stage because it had not been raised in the courts below and involved disputed questions of fact; it did not prevent the decree for possession in this title-based suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished the reliance on Gyan Chand v. K.B. Lal and Ors. because this was a suit for possession based on title, not an eviction suit under the Rent Act. It considered Sections 13 and 13A of the Rent Act but held that the protection plea, never raised below and involving disputed facts, could not be entertained for the first time in the appeal. The Court also noted that the denial of the claimant’s title had been found proved.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and title_based_possession_suit and rent_protection_not_pleaded_below and rent_protection_depends_on_disputed_facts

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal from decisions of lower courts.
predicates.title_based_possession_suit: The underlying suit sought possession on the basis of the claimant’s title rather than as an eviction proceeding under rent-control law.
predicates.rent_protection_not_pleaded_below: The occupants did not raise a claim to statutory rent protection in the lower courts.
predicates.rent_protection_depends_on_disputed_fact: Determining whether the occupants qualify for statutory rent protection requires resolution of disputed facts.

issues.definition: In a special-leave appeal arising from a title-based possession suit, a rent-protection claim that was not raised below and depends on disputed facts cannot be entertained for the first time.
